success_criterion: AGENTS.md 'Success criterion: iterative improvement of the index-calculus baseline'
question: On E0/F_2^19 (EC1N19Ckb1h01617b86df6c, r = 130873), does replacing the tau6 arm's per-shift PolyBoRi solve (TauField.system + ideal + groebner_basis + variety) by a native enumeration of the same variety lower the end-to-end cold CPU cost of one complete, verified ECDLP, with every target, every shift system, every relation and every log unchanged?

current_baseline.row: docs/ic/BASELINES.md n=19 (volcano-ic tau-orbit dim-6 base, Sage Groebner, arm tau6)

cost_structure_of_the_baseline.setup_note: built once, outside every timed interval of that run
cost_structure_of_the_baseline.rank_stage: none: relations are collected for one target (R = aP + bQ), there is no reusable table
cost_structure_of_the_baseline.reading: the per-shift Groebner solve (system construction + PolyBoRi GB + variety, the interval gb_cpu_s) is 99.4% of the tau6 arm's CPU; it is the lever

curve.generator: run.sage generator(cur, "E0"); must equal the archived P of runtime-info.json

change.summary: tauRelation's variety per shift j comes from native/src/lib.rs (Rust cdylib, ctypes) instead of Sage. Everything else is tau.sage's code: tauDlp (rng, targets, shift order, matrix, left kernel, verification) is called unchanged with the global tauRelation rebound to tauRelationNative, whose loop is tauRelation's line for line after the variety. Setup builds NativeTauField (no Boolean ring or shift systems) for TauCurve.
change.exactness_argument: TauField.system(j, xR, b) is, coordinate by coordinate over GF(2^19), S3(x1, x2, xR) = (x1 x2)^2 + xR^2 (x1^2 + x2^2) + xR x1 x2 + b with x1 = sum u_i z^i and x2 = sigma^j(sum w_l z^l); its variety over F_2 is the set of (u, w) in F_2^6 x F_2^6 with S3 = 0. The native code decides all 4,096 pairs (S3 is affine-linear in w for fixed u, and its coefficients are affine in u), so it returns the whole variety, as a set (ascending (u, w)). The order of a multi-solution variety is the only freedom: an exhaustive local survey of all (xR, j) finds 2,375 such systems (2,001 shift-0 swaps (a, b), (b, a)); on this panel and the archived scalars the candidate meets 26, all shift-0 swaps, whose order changes no count, relation or matrix row (only the order of the two terms), so the gates compare rows and multiset decompositions across B and N (smoke/multi_survey.json, smoke/multi_calls.json).
change.native_tests: cargo test (solve == direct form == brute force S3)

arms.B: baseline: unmodified tau.sage (Sage Groebner per shift); its own process per point
arms.N: candidate: tau.sage tauDlp with tauRelationNative; its own process per point
arms.Naa: A/A control: a second process of N per point
arms.NX: planted positive control: N plus the work it removes, redone: every shift system is also built and solved by Sage (TauField.system, groebner_basis, variety) and compared with the native variety as a set (abort on any difference), then discarded
arms.rho: matched signed-Frobenius rho of rho-arm-20261014 (rho_frob.py SageBackend, R = 16, 64 reps per point, walk seeds rho-arm-20261014:walk:k); S unit and gap only, never decides

design.panel: inputs/panel.json (role n19-native-heldout-v1, make_panel.py): 16 new scalars, none equal to, the negative of or a Frobenius image of an archived scalar or of each other
design.rng: tauDlp rng = random.Random(panel rng_seed) in every IC arm of a point, so B, N, Naa and NX draw the same targets and shift orders
design.schedule: schedule.json (make_schedule.py): S0 selftest, O1 archived exactness, then P00..P15, one segment per point with B, N, Naa, NX, rho in random.Random(2026101919 + i) order
design.process_model: one fresh Sage process per row, CPU affinity one CPU (the lowest allowed), one runner
design.environment: GitHub ubuntu-24.04 runner; sagemath/sagemath:10.10@sha256:310dfe23fc786f3a5a06a7b0387c60201ec79b32c0db941b7624505ee5edb565 (the baseline run's image); native library built on the runner by the pinned Rust toolchain before the schedule
design.time_guard: skip a segment (rows skipped_time_guard, verdict invalid) if elapsed + its upper estimate exceeds 300 min; a failed S0 or O1 stops the schedule before any timed segment
design.runtime_estimate: about 45 min: B about 40-55 s and NX about the same per point, N and Naa about 1 s, rho about 1 s, Sage start-up a few s per process

intervals.clock: time.process_time() (CPU, the baseline row's measure); perf_counter wall co-reported; each row records time.get_clock_info("process_time").resolution
intervals.setup: target-independent construction: field (TauField for B and NX, NativeTauField for N/Naa), TauCurve (V' base and orbit representatives), the native context for N/Naa/NX (dlopen + tau6_new) and the generator
intervals.online: tauDlp: first target-dependent operation (tauEigen, R = aP + bQ) .. verified log (s * P == Q); relation search, matrix, left kernel and verification
intervals.cold: setup + online, one process, one point; Sage import and source loading precede it and are recorded by the launcher (launcher_wall_s), not charged to either arm
intervals.fixture: Q = s * P is built between setup and online, outside both (as in rho-arm-20261014)
intervals.online_separability: n = 19 has no reusable factor-log table: every relation contains Q, so the one-target pipeline is setup (target independent) + online (everything else). Both are timed separately in every process; online is the per-target cost and S_online is reported per arm. The repeated-batch measurement below covers the case where a per-process interval is too short to read
intervals.repeated_batch: pre-registered secondary, labelled "repeated-batch, warm": every N and Naa process, after its cold interval is recorded, rebuilds setup 20 times and reruns the same point's tauDlp 3 times (same rng seed; the relations must repeat) and reports the mean per repetition. It never decides and never replaces a cold number

statistics.primary: R = mean over points of cold_cpu_s(B) / mean over points of cold_cpu_s(N)
statistics.interval: paired bootstrap over the 16 points (B and N of a point drawn together), 10,000 draws, numpy default_rng(20261019), 2.5/97.5 percentiles (stats.py)
statistics.primary_is: the END-TO-END cold ratio (setup + online); online, setup, wall, launcher wall and the per-call solve ratio are co-reported and never decide
secondary: online and setup ratios B/N, cold wall ratio, launcher wall ratio (Sage start-up included)
solve ms per shift system per arm (gb_cpu_s / gb_calls)
phase shares of N: native solve, rest of the relation search, linear algebra, setup
S = cpu / (u * sqrt(r)) with u = rho CPU per group operation of this run (the row's unit): S cold, S online, S setup per arm, rho S cold
cold gap to the matched rho: geometric mean over points of cold_cpu_s / rho cpu per solve, bootstrap interval
the repeated-batch warm setup and online means of N and Naa

decision_rule.improvement: R 95% lower bound > 1 (the native tau6 solve becomes the n=19 end-to-end cold baseline)
decision_rule.invalid: any gate or control fails, or any scheduled row is missing (time-guard skips included)

controls.aa: mean cold_cpu_s(N) / mean cold_cpu_s(Naa) inside aa_window
controls.planted: R_plant = mean cold(NX) / mean cold(N), paired bootstrap as the primary: 95% lower bound > 1

gates: every scheduled row ran, exit 0, verified (log == scalar mod r and s * P == Q)
S0: on 300 random (xR, j) systems (j = t mod 19), the Sage variety of TauField.system equals the native variety as a set and the native brute-force S3 enumeration equals the native output
O1: the candidate on the ten archived scalars with the archived rng seeds reproduces run 38520305068's tau6 targets, gb_calls, spurious, relations and log, and the archived generator P
per point: targets, gb_calls, spurious, relations and log identical across B, N, Naa and NX

per point: the relation rows (column -> sum sign lambda^e mod r, i.e. the matrix tauDlp builds) and the decompositions as multisets of (column, sign, Frobenius power) identical across B, N, Naa and NX (sha256); the ordered lists are recorded for all and must be identical across N, Naa, NX
per point: NX compared every shift system with Sage (checked_calls == gb_calls), no mismatch
per point: the generator equals the archived P; rho 64/64 verified; the warm batch repeats the relations
one pinned CPU for every process; one native library digest across every native process
multiplicity: one primary statistic; every secondary is descriptive and never changes the verdict

power.note: the expected effect (local diagnostics: per-call solve 14 us native against 7.4 ms archived Sage) is far above min_delta; min_delta 1.20 is the smallest effect the protocol is sized to detect

tier: Tier 1 in the n = 83 sense: one fresh GitHub-hosted runner, one pinned CPU, one fresh process per row, CPU-only. Not isolab; one host class; not replayed
what_is_not_claimed: nothing about rho: the matched rho is the same Python/Sage walk as the baseline row and is not tuned for wall time
no advance in the exponent: the change is engineering (the same algorithm, the same relations); the counts of the IC are unchanged by construction
